digest.component_or_area: LLM model class resolution and provider qualification
propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical Bedrock ids like 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' are treated as already-qualified strings and returned unmodified).
The provider qualifier test incorrectly uses 'colon in model' to detect provider-qualified strings, conflating the version separator colon with the provider:model delimiter colon.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked first before scanning the model string, so no punctuation in the model id can overrule or silently discard the configuration.
Conflicting inline qualifiers and configured providers must raise LLMConfigError rather than silently picking a winner, since either choice discards an explicit instruction.

The decision of whether a string is already provider-qualified must be made by a single shared function consulted by both _resolve_target and infer_provider to prevent drift between the two implementations.

Provider name detection should validate against the registered provider set rather than a shape/pattern rule, so future providers require no code edits and unknown providers produce diagnostics naming the invalid and valid options.
